findings.title: `getClientsWithPermission` returns empty set for per-client permissions because individual client resources have no type
findings.body: `getClientsWithPermission(String scope)` queries `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)`. However, when a permission is created for a specific client, `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` (line 104) creates the resource via `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId())` without setting its `type` (only the 'all-clients' resource created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.init` has `resource.setType(type)`). As a result, `findByType` will never find per-client resources, and `getClientsWithPermission` will only ever match the `Clients` resource-type resource (returning the literal string `"Clients"`, which is not a client ID) instead of the IDs of clients with granted permissions. In `ClientsResource.getClients`, when `canView()` is false, this causes the client list to be empty even when the caller has `view`, `configure`, or `manage` permissions on individual clients (note that in `PermissionClientTest.testManageOnlyOneClient`, `findAll()` only passed because `myclient` has `alwaysDisplayInConsole` or similar, or `view` wasn't tested with a non-console client).

findings.title: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName` does not handle `CLIENTS` resource type
findings.body: `getResourceName(KeycloakSession, Policy, Resource)` only checks `if (USERS.getType().equals(resourceType))` to resolve the human-readable name (returning `"All users"` or `user.getUsername()`), and falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()` for `CLIENTS`. Because client resources are created with the client's internal UUID as `name` and no `displayName`, representations of policies/permissions for `Clients` will return `null` (or the internal UUID) as the resource name instead of `"All clients"` or `client.getClientId()`.

findings.title: `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` ignores `all-clients` permission when a per-client resource exists for a different scope
findings.body: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope)`, if a resource for `client.getId()` exists in `resourceStore` (for example, because a permission was created on that specific client for `map-roles`), `resource` is non-null at line 215, so the `all-clients` (`CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE`) resource is never evaluated. If the caller was granted `view` or `manage` via an `all-clients` permission, `hasPermission(client, VIEW)` or `hasPermission(client, MANAGE)` (when called via `canConfigure(client)` or `canManage(client)`) will evaluate only the per-client resource and falsely return `false`. Compare with `UserPermissionsV2`, which evaluates both the specific resource and the resource-type resource (or combines their permissions).

findings.title: `isPermissionsEnabled` and `getAccess` in `ClientPermissionsV2` break `ClientResource.getClient` when FGAP V2 is enabled
findings.body: `ClientPermissionsV2` overrides `isPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel)` to throw `UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`, while inheriting `getAccess(ClientModel)` from `ClientPermissions`. When `ClientResource.getClient()` (i.e. `GET /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id}`) is called, it invokes `auth.clients().getAccess(client)` which works, and if `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` is also enabled or if any admin endpoint calls `isPermissionsEnabled`, it will throw an unhandled `UnsupportedOperationException` (HTTP 500). Furthermore, `ClientPermissions.canView()` (called by `super.canList()`) or other inherited methods in `ClientPermissions` must be checked to ensure they don't call unsupported V1 methods.
